summary: Defines a Subscriber-ID suboption for the DHCP relay agent information option. It lets a relay agent attach a stable subscriber identifier to client messages, independent of the client and the underlying network hardware.

eli5.summary: A tag that stays with a customer's requests no matter which device or line they use, so the provider always knows whose they are.

questions: what is the dhcp subscriber-id suboption
what is dhcp relay agent option 82 suboption 6
how does dhcp identify a subscriber
why use subscriber-id instead of circuit-id
subtitle: A DHCP relay agent suboption that carries a stable subscriber ID, whatever network path the customer uses.

tldr.problem: Relay agents tag DHCP messages with the Circuit-ID and Remote-ID suboptions, but those values depend on the physical network, so they change when a customer connects by a different path.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3993 defines the Subscriber-ID suboption (code 6), an ASCII string assigned by the provider, which a relay agent can add to relayed DHCP messages.
tldr.outcome: The provider's DHCP server can recognize a subscriber independent of the access network and treat it as additional input when choosing an address and settings. Fraudulent relay data remains a risk.

today: RFC 3993 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the relay agent option from RFC 3046.

sections.title: Why a Subscriber-ID Is Needed
sections.content:
DHCP (RFC 2131) gives IPv4 clients addresses and configuration. A relay agent receives broadcast messages from clients and forwards them to DHCP servers as unicast. In networks such as DOCSIS data-over-cable and xDSL, relays add information using the relay agent information option (RFC 3046). Servers that recognize it echo it back, and may use it in deciding which addresses and parameters a client gets.

RFC 3046 defines the Remote-ID and Circuit-ID suboptions. Their values usually come from a network resource, such as the IP address of an access device, an ATM Virtual Circuit identifier or a DOCSIS cable-modem identifier. So they depend on the physical network, and a client that connects by a different path produces different values.
sections.eli5: The old labels say which wire a request came in on. If the customer plugs into a different wire, the label changes, which is confusing for the provider.

sections.title: What the Subscriber-ID Means
sections.content:
The Subscriber-ID suboption carries a value that can be independent of the physical network the subscriber uses. It complements the network-based suboptions and might be used alongside them. The provider-assigned subscriber-id is meant to stay stable as customers connect through different paths and as the network changes.

It lets the provider assign or activate subscriber-specific actions, such as assigning a host IP address and subnet mask, DNS configuration, or triggering accounting. Because it is decoupled from the access network's structure, a subscriber moving from one access point to another would not require reconfiguration at the provider's DHCP servers.

The meaning of the string is provider-specific. The RFC sets no semantic requirements on its contents.
sections.eli5: It is a membership number. Wherever you sit, you show the same number, so the provider knows you and does not need to redo your settings.

sections.title: The Suboption Format
sections.content:
The suboption looks like many other relay information suboptions: a code, a length, and the value.

The Code is 6. The one-octet Len field is the length of the ID string in octets, and the minimum length of the string is 1 octet. The Subscriber-ID itself is an NVT ASCII string. It MUST NOT be NULL terminated, because the length is already given in the Len field.
sections.eli5: It is a small package: a number saying what kind it is, a number saying how long it is, then the customer's name tag in plain letters.

sections.title: Relay Agent and Server Behavior
sections.content:
DHCP relay agents MAY be configured to include a Subscriber-ID suboption if they include a relay agent information option in relayed DHCP messages. How the subscriber-id strings are assigned and configured is outside the scope of the RFC.

On the server side, the suboption is extra information. A server configured to support it may use it, together with other relay agent option data and the options in the client's messages, to assign an IP address or other configuration parameters. There is no special additional processing for this suboption.
sections.eli5: The helper in the middle may stick the tag on the request. The provider's server can read the tag as one more hint when deciding what settings to hand out.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
The relay agent option depends on a trusted relationship between the relay agent and the server. Fraudulent relay agent option data could lead to theft of service or exhaustion of limited resources like IP addresses by unauthorized clients. A host that tampered with another host's relay data could deny it service or lead the server to assign it inappropriate parameters.

A perimeter defense can block these options unless the relay is trusted, but the RFC says a deeper defense using the Authentication Suboption or IPSec SHOULD be deployed as well. Message authentication for DHCP is defined in RFC 3118.

Depending on the identifier chosen, a Subscriber-ID may identify a specific host or user. In practice DHCP messages are usually confined to the provider's internal network, but if they leave it or values become visible to other users, privacy concerns may arise. Administrators should pick appropriate identifiers.
sections.eli5: If someone fakes the tag, they could get free service or use up addresses, so the relay and server must trust each other. Tags should also not reveal private things about a person.

sections.title: IANA Assignment
sections.content: IANA assigned the value 6 from the DHCP Relay Agent Information Option suboption codes to the Subscriber-ID suboption. That is the only IANA action in the RFC.
sections.eli5: The official number list now says that number 6 means the customer tag, so everyone uses the same number.

fields.name: Len
fields.desc: Length of the ID string in octets; minimum 1.

fields.name: Subscriber-ID string
fields.desc: NVT ASCII string, not NULL terminated; variable length.
